Action-result wording rather than duty lists
Inclusion of client or stakeholder testimonials
Links to portfolio or project evidence

sections.name: Education & Qualifications

improver: Inclusion of thesis or major project title

sections.name: Impact
sections.description: How the scholarship will help and what outcome it enables, ideally connected to a broader community or long-term benefit.
improver: Clear key performance indicators (KPIs) for post-scholarship outcomes
Alignment with national or regional development goals
Plan for knowledge sharing with peers
Commitment to mentorship of future applicants
Inclusion of a sustainability statement for funded activities
Outline of measurable social return on investment

fields.name: need_or_merit
fields.label: Need or merit basis
fields.placeholder: first in family to attend university, regional background

missing_detail_rules.reason: TED tailors the application to the specific scholarship's purpose and criteria.
The applicant profile section needs to name the specific field of study.
Scholarship applications are tied to a specific institution and program, not study in general.
Without a stated need or merit basis, TED will write a general case that's easy for you to sharpen with your real circumstances.

recommendation_reason: A specific, evidence-led application stands out far more than a generic one.

name: Statement of Purpose
plain_description: An academic purpose statement for graduate, postgraduate, or research program applications.

sections.name: Academic Focus
sections.description: Your intended field of study and the specific topic that draws you to it — ideally framed around a real research question or intellectual motivation, not just general interest.

sections.name: Preparation
sections.description: The academic or professional background that's prepared you for this — courses, projects, or experience that built the specific ability this area calls for.
vital: Specific coursework, projects, or roles that prepared the applicant
What each experience taught that is relevant to the program

sections.name: Program Fit
sections.description: Why this specific program is the right fit, naming the faculty, labs, courses, or institutional strengths that genuinely set it apart from alternatives.
vital: Clear reason the specific program is appropriate
Named features of the program (units, staff, facilities, structure)
Why those features suit this applicant over alternatives

sections.name: Future Direction
sections.description: Your career or research goal after completion, and the contribution you intend to make to your field or community.
vital: Career or research goal after completion
A defined career or research goal after completion
The step-wise link from program to that goal

fields.name: field_of_interest
fields.label: Your intended field and topic of interest

fields.name: relevant_background
fields.label: Relevant academic or professional background
fields.placeholder: two years as a community health worker

missing_detail_rules.reason: The program-fit section can't be written without knowing the specific program.
Without a specific field and topic, the academic focus section reads as generic enthusiasm rather than genuine direction.
The preparation section needs real background to draw on, not a placeholder claim of being 'well prepared'.

recommendation_reason: Admissions panels read these closely for genuine fit, not generic enthusiasm.

name: Study Plan
plain_description: A practical plan for coursework, exam prep, or self-directed learning.

sections.name: Learning Goal
sections.description: What you're building competence in, by when, and how success will be measured — a real deadline and metric, not a vague intention.

sections.name: Current Level
sections.description: Your current strengths and the priority gaps that need attention, named honestly rather than glossed over.

sections.name: Weekly Schedule
sections.description: What each week of study actually involves — hours, a practice task, and a review method, not just 'study more'.

sections.name: Accountability
sections.description: When progress gets checked and against what measure, so the plan adjusts based on how it's actually going rather than running on autopilot.

missing_detail_rules.reason: The schedule and gaps only make sense once TED knows the specific subject.
A study plan without a real deadline can't set a realistic weekly pace.
Naming specific gaps lets TED prioritise the schedule around what actually needs the work — without them TED will suggest a general structure.

recommendation_reason: A written plan turns vague study intentions into a schedule you'll actually follow.

name: Research Proposal
plain_description: A research plan for honours, masters, PhD, or coursework research — title, question, method, and expected contribution.

sections.name: Research Title and Question
sections.description: A working title and a central research question, specific enough that it could actually be answered rather than a broad area of interest.

sections.name: Background and Rationale
sections.description: Why this topic matters and the gap in existing work it responds to, grounded in real context rather than a general claim of importance.

sections.name: Methodology
sections.description: The method, the data source or participant group, and the analysis approach — concrete enough that a supervisor could assess feasibility.

sections.name: Expected Contribution
sections.description: The academic or practical value this research is expected to contribute, and to whom.
vital: Academic or practical value of the research
The gap in existing knowledge the research addresses
Who benefits from the findings and how

fields.name: research_topic
fields.label: Research topic
fields.placeholder: early intervention in regional youth mental health

fields.name: research_question
fields.label: Central research question
fields.placeholder: what barriers prevent regional youth from accessing early mental health support?

missing_detail_rules.reason: Every section of a research proposal is built around the specific topic and question.
A proposal needs an answerable question, not just a topic area, or the methodology section has nothing to respond to.
Naming a method gives the methodology section something real to build on — without it TED will suggest a plausible method common to this kind of research.

recommendation_reason: A clear proposal is what supervisors and panels actually assess before approving research.

name: Literature Review
plain_description: An academic review that summarises existing sources on a topic and establishes the gap your work addresses.

sections.name: Review Scope
sections.description: The topic and the specific themes this review focuses on, with clear boundaries rather than an attempt to cover everything written on the subject.
improver: transparent reporting of search strategy steps
PRISMA flow diagram to illustrate source selection
summary table of excluded studies with reasons
statement of language and publication type limits

sections.name: Key Themes
sections.description: The main themes or schools of thought in the literature, with what different scholars actually argue rather than a generic summary.
vital: Main themes or schools of thought
Key authors or studies representing each theme
How the themes relate to the review's research question
improver: discussion of cultural or regional variations

sections.name: Debate or Tension
sections.description: Where the literature genuinely disagrees or remains uncertain, described fairly with the contrasting positions named.
vital: The competing positions and who holds them
Why the disagreement matters for the field or the research question
improver: use of direct quotations to capture nuance
assessment of citation impact for each stance
mapping of debate across publication years
suggestion of future research to resolve tension

sections.name: Gap and Direction
sections.description: The gap that remains in existing work, and the specific research direction this project takes in response to it.
improver: explicit statement of contribution to policy
discussion of limitations to frame gap
proposal of measurable outcomes for the new work

fields.name: review_topic
fields.label: Topic of the review
fields.placeholder: remote learning outcomes in regional Australia

fields.name: key_themes
fields.label: Themes you already know you want to cover
fields.placeholder: digital access, teacher workload, student engagement

missing_detail_rules.reason: The themes and gap can't be identified without a defined topic to review.
Naming themes you already know matter helps TED structure the review around your actual focus — without them TED will infer likely themes from the topic.

recommendation_reason: A clear literature review shows you understand the field well enough to know where the gap actually is.

name: Academic Appeal Letter
plain_description: A formal, evidence-led appeal against a grade, exclusion, or other academic decision.

sections.name: Decision Being Appealed
sections.description: The exact decision being appealed, the date it was made, and the course or program it relates to — stated factually, not as a complaint about fairness.
improver: Reference to specific assessment component or module

sections.name: Grounds for Appeal
sections.description: The specific grounds for the appeal — a marking error, a procedural issue, or special circumstances — supported by the evidence behind it.
improver: Citation of exact grading rubric section
Inclusion of expert opinion or second opinion
Use of bullet points for each ground
Clear linkage between evidence and each ground
Brief justification of why the ground is applicable

sections.name: Explanation
sections.description: What happened, when, and how it affected your work, set out factually, including any steps you took at the time to manage the situation.
improver: Specific dates and times for key incidents
Reference to supporting emails or letters
Use of concise paragraphs with topic sentences
Inclusion of any mitigating factors beyond medical evidence

sections.name: Requested Outcome
sections.description: The specific outcome you're requesting, stated plainly so the panel knows exactly what's being asked for.
vital: The specific remedy requested (re-mark, re-enrolment, waiver)
improver: Clear statement of preferred remedy first
Justification linking requested outcome to grounds
Optional secondary remedy if primary denied
Expression of appreciation for panel's consideration
Professional closing with full contact details
Signature line with printed name and student ID

fields.name: appeal_grounds
fields.label: Your grounds for appeal
fields.placeholder: marking error / special circumstances / procedural issue

fields.name: circumstances
fields.label: What happened and when
fields.placeholder: a medical issue during the exam period, documented by my GP

fields.name: requested_outcome
fields.label: The outcome you're requesting
fields.placeholder: a re-mark of the final exam

missing_detail_rules.reason: An appeal has to name the exact decision being challenged, not a general grievance.
Most universities only accept appeals on specific grounds (marking error, procedural unfairness, or special circumstances) — TED needs to know which applies so the letter argues the right case.
The explanation section needs real, factual circumstances — without them the appeal has no substance behind its grounds.
A specific requested outcome makes the appeal actionable for the panel — without one TED will draft a reasonable default request you can adjust.

recommendation_reason: A factual, evidence-led appeal that sticks to specific grounds gets taken far more seriously than a general complaint about fairness.

name: Extension Request Letter
plain_description: A formal request for more time on an assignment or assessment.

sections.name: Opening Request
sections.description: The assignment, the course, and the current due date — named specifically so there's no ambiguity about what's being requested.
improver: Mention of any prior extension granted

sections.name: Reason
sections.description: The genuine circumstance affecting your ability to meet the deadline, explained factually without over-justifying.
vital: When the circumstance occurred and how it affected the work
Any supporting evidence available (medical certificate, employer letter)
improver: Explanation of alignment with extenuating circumstances policy

sections.name: Proposed Date
sections.description: A specific revised submission date that realistically allows you to finish what's left, not just 'a bit more time'.
vital: A realistic new date with brief justification for the length asked
improver: Confirmation of access to required resources by new date
Statement of contingency plan if further delay occurs
Reference to university's standard extension windows
Inclusion of brief apology for delay within this section

sections.name: Close
sections.description: Thanks, and a mention of any supporting evidence you can provide if relevant.
improver: Inclusion of student phone number for contact
Offer to meet in person to discuss
Willingness to accept alternative assessment format

fields.name: reason
fields.label: The reason for your request
fields.placeholder: a family medical emergency this week

missing_detail_rules.reason: An extension request has to name the specific assignment.
The proposed new date only makes sense relative to the original deadline.
A genuine, stated reason is what makes the request more than a generic ask for more time.
A specific proposed date makes the request concrete — without one TED will suggest a reasonable default based on the circumstance described.

recommendation_reason: A clear, early extension request is far more likely to be granted than a late, vague one.

name: Student Support Plan
plain_description: A practical plan for academic, wellbeing, accessibility, or attendance support.

sections.name: Student Context
sections.description: The student's course or year level and the area support is needed in — anchored to a real situation, not a generic support category.

sections.name: Strengths
sections.description: The student's genuine strengths and any existing supports or strategies already working, not just a list of deficits.
vital: Strengths stated specifically enough to build strategies on
Existing supports already in place (people, services, adjustments)

sections.name: Support Needs

vital: Each need described with its impact on learning or participation
Priority order when there are multiple needs

sections.name: Actions and Review

missing_detail_rules.reason: The actions in this plan are specific to the kind of support being arranged.
The student context section needs a real course or year level to anchor the plan.
Naming what's already working keeps the plan from reading as purely deficit-focused — without it TED will write a more neutral strengths section.

recommendation_reason: A written plan makes sure support is consistent and doesn't depend on one person remembering it.

name: Course Comparison Matrix
plain_description: A decision matrix comparing courses, universities, or training providers before you choose.

sections.name: Options
sections.description: The specific options being compared, named clearly so the comparison is grounded in real choices rather than generic alternatives.
vital: At least 2 named courses or programs with provider
Key facts per option (duration, cost, delivery mode, entry requirements)
improver: Tuition fee breakdown (fees, taxes, additional costs)
Campus facilities relevant to the course

sections.name: Criteria
sections.description: The decision criteria that actually matter for this choice — cost, duration, delivery mode, reputation, and career outcomes among the likely candidates.
vital: Criteria weighted or ordered by importance to the decision-maker
At least 3 criteria covering cost, outcome, and practicality
improver: Scenario analysis for different budget levels
Employer demand trends for the skillset

sections.name: Comparison Notes
sections.description: Each option's real strengths and weaknesses, set out honestly rather than treating every option as equally good.
vital: Relative strengths or weaknesses of each option
A clear front-runner or the trade-off blocking the decision

sections.name: Recommendation

missing_detail_rules.reason: TED can't build a comparison without knowing the specific options on the table.
Knowing your real priorities lets TED weight the comparison toward what matters to you — without them TED will use commonly-weighted criteria.

recommendation_reason: Laying options out side by side makes a hard decision much easier to actually make.

name: Academic Reference Request
plain_description: A respectful request to a teacher, lecturer, or supervisor for an academic reference.

sections.name: Opening Request
sections.description: What you're applying for and the specific reference you're asking for, stated clearly so the referee knows exactly what's needed.
improver: Reference to a notable achievement to highlight
Mention intended audience for the reference
Suggest approximate word count for the reference

sections.name: Relationship Context
sections.description: How they know your work and over what period — the course or unit, the timeframe, and what you actually did during that time.
improver: Highlight any awards or recognitions received
Reference feedback comments from the referee

sections.name: Application Context
sections.description: What the opportunity is looking for, so your referee knows what to emphasise rather than guessing.

Identify key competencies the panel seeks
Provide a brief anecdote illustrating fit
Propose a concise closing endorsement line

Offer to reciprocate with a reference for them
Include a brief personal sign-off with full name

fields.label: The course/unit and what you worked on together

Knowing the specific opportunity helps your referee know what to emphasise.
The relationship-context section needs to name real shared work, not a vague 'I studied with you'.

name: Profit & Loss Statement
plain_description: A profit and loss statement showing revenue, costs, and net profit for a reporting period -- the source document a Financial Review is built from.

sections.name: Revenue
sections.description: Total revenue or sales for the period, broken down by major revenue stream where there is more than one.
vital: Total revenue or sales for the period
a breakdown by major revenue stream if there is more than one
improver: Comparison to the prior period or budget
a split between one-off and recurring revenue
Visual bar chart of revenue streams
Narrative on market drivers affecting sales
Commentary on currency impact on revenue

sections.name: Cost of Goods Sold & Gross Profit
sections.description: The direct costs of delivering the product or service, and the resulting gross profit.
vital: Cost of goods sold (direct costs tied to delivering the product or service)
improver: Impact of inventory write-downs on COGS
Comparison of gross margin to prior year average
Highlight any one-off cost events affecting COGS
Risk assessment of key raw-material price volatility

sections.name: Operating Expenses
sections.description: Operating expense categories such as wages, rent, marketing, and admin, with an amount for each.
vital: Operating expense categories (e.g. wages, rent, marketing, admin)
improver: a split between one-off and recurring expenses
Narrative on staffing level changes driving wage expense
Highlight of lease vs. owned asset cost implications
Year-over-year variance analysis for each major expense
Forecast of operating expense trends for next period
Identification of regulatory compliance cost impacts

sections.name: Net Profit Summary
sections.description: Net profit or loss for the period, calculated as gross profit minus operating expenses.
vital: Net profit or loss for the period, calculated as gross profit minus operating expenses
The reporting period the figure covers
Whether the figure is before or after tax
improver: a brief explanation of what drove the result
Visual summary of profit drivers in infographic form
Commentary on tax provision impact on net profit
Sensitivity of net profit to key cost assumptions
Benchmark net profit against industry average
Highlight of any one-off gains or losses affecting net profit
Forward-looking profit outlook with scenario notes

fields.name: operating_expenses_total
fields.label: Total operating expenses for the period

missing_detail_rules.reason: A profit and loss statement is always anchored to a specific period -- the figures only make sense in that context.
Revenue is the starting line of any P&L; without it none of the downstream figures (gross profit, net profit) can be calculated.
Service businesses with no direct delivery cost may not have a COGS figure -- if absent, gross profit is treated as equal to revenue.
Net profit cannot be calculated without total operating expenses for the period.

recommendation_reason: A clear profit and loss statement is the foundation for every other financial document -- budgets, reviews, and funding proposals all draw from it.
